books.title: The Number Devil
books.author: Hans Magnus Enzensberger
books.why: Turns twelve nights of dreams into a tour of number ideas, from primes to infinity, with no textbook feel.

books.title: Lauren Ipsum
books.author: Carlos Bueno
books.why: Hides the ideas behind computer science, like recursion and functions, inside a storybook journey through a strange land.

books.title: The Phantom Tollbooth
books.author: Norton Juster
books.why: Turns a bored kid's drive through a tollbooth into a play on words and logic that makes thinking feel like an adventure.

books.title: What Is the Name of This Book?
books.author: Raymond Smullyan
books.why: A stack of knights, knaves and liar puzzles that trains the same cross-it-off deduction used in the Think track.

books.title: Aha! Insight
books.author: Martin Gardner
books.why: Short puzzles built to reward the flash of seeing a clever shortcut instead of grinding through a long method.

books.title: Ada Byron Lovelace and the Thinking Machine
books.author: Laurie Wallmark
books.why: Shows the first programmer imagining what a machine could do long before one existed to try it on.

books.title: Alan Turing (Little People, BIG DREAMS)
books.author: Maria Isabel Sanchez Vegara
books.why: Tells the story of a boy who loved puzzles and grew up to build a machine that broke a code.

books.title: Who Was Albert Einstein?
books.author: Jess Brallier
books.why: Shows how he kept asking simple questions about light and time until they finally had answers.

books.title: Hello Ruby
books.author: Linda Liukas
books.why: Introduces sorting, sequencing and pattern ideas through a picture-book adventure a very young child can follow.

books.title: Sophie's World
books.author: Jostein Gaarder
books.why: Walks through the history of philosophy as a mystery story, for whenever the debate track is ready to go deeper.
